tagline: Beside the lake, then up to the Divide.
intro: Out of West Glacier, the road runs up the valley of Lake McDonald and climbs toward Logan Pass. The pavement narrows and winds, with hairpin turns west of the pass. Along the Garden Wall, Thomas Vint's alignment cut down the switchbacks and the road's mark on the mountainside. A crossing that once took several days now takes a few hours.

Up to 80 feet of snow can lie on the pass in spring, and the plow crews need about ten weeks to open the road, some days clearing as little as 500 feet. The vintage red buses that tour it are still called Jammers, after drivers who had to jam the gearbox into low.

moments.title: Lake McDonald
moments.text: The road keeps to the southern shore of Lake McDonald, about ten miles long, which fills a valley shaped by erosion and glaciers.

moments.title: Weeping Wall
moments.text: Snowmelt seeps from the side of Haystack Butte and the Garden Wall beside the road.

moments.title: Logan Pass
moments.text: The road crosses the Continental Divide here at 6,646 feet, its high point; just east of the pass, the Big Drift often gathers more than 100 feet of snow.

practical: Logan Pass closes in winter. Between Avalanche Creek and Rising Sun, vehicles are limited to 21 feet long and 8 feet wide, and vehicles over 10 feet high may not clear the rock overhangs driving west between Logan Pass and the Loop.
